{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABepnbvw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIK1cY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 362, "title": "Reorganize Add Node into five categories (separate AI Models) and auto-sort names", "body": "## Goal

Simplify the **Graph Editor → Add Node** picker by replacing the ambiguous categories with five clearly defined groups, **separating AI-inference Nodes from ordinary deterministic processors**, and automatically sorting Node display names **alphabetically / Japanese 五十音順 (gojūon order)** within each group.

The user should never have to remember the source-code insertion order or wonder whether a utility belongs in Processors. Keep the picker minimal: no sort button, extra description, manual count, or redundant helper UI.

## Desired categories and order

1. **Sources / inputs** — inputs and constant sources, including Chrome tab audio, Microphone audio, Button, Text, Number.
2. **AI Models** — Nodes that actually execute AI-model inference, e.g. ReazonSpeech, Whisper, Zipformer, Parakeet, Moonshine, OPUS-MT (both directions), TranslateGemma (both directions), Text Summary (both models), IfCondition, Supertonic 3 TTS, Kokoro TTS, Qwen3-TTS, CosyVoice3. Classify by **whether inference is performed**, not whether there is exactly one Node per downloaded model (some model assets serve multiple Node types).
3. **Processors** — normal non-AI processing / formatting / buffering / transformation, including Text formatter, Text accumulator, Text sliding window, Text window, Hold, keyed text pairing/coalescing/accumulation and similar utilities.
4. **Outputs** — sinks such as Display, Speaker, Audio player / WAV, Focused input text output.
5. **Subgraphs** — user-defined subgraphs.

**Remove the `Constants / utilities` category completely.** Move its current special cases: `Number` and `Text` to Sources / inputs; `TextFormatter` and `Hold` to Processors.

Within **each** category, sort Node options by their **user-visible `definition.label`** using a **deterministic Japanese-aware alphabetical / kana collation** (e.g. `Intl.Collator('ja-JP', { usage: 'sort', sensitivity: 'base', numeric: true })`, with sensible stable tie-breaks). This should be consistent with the sorting convention requested for Models in [#352](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/352).

## Current implementation

[extension/graph-editor.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-editor.js):

- The category selector currently contains `All categories`, `Sources / inputs`, `Processors`, `Constants / utilities`, `Outputs`, `Subgraphs`.
- `filterPalette()` determines category via an ad-hoc rule:
  ```js
  const category = type.startsWith('Subgraph:') ? 'Subgraphs' : ['Number', 'Text', 'TextFormatter', 'Hold'].includes(type) ? 'Constants / utilities'
    : !Object.keys(definition.inputs).length ? 'Sources / inputs'
    : !Object.keys(definition.outputs).length ? 'Outputs' : 'Processors';
  ```
- The category group entries and their options currently follow `NODE_TYPES` / library-definition iteration order, rather than name-based sorting.
- Because many AI nodes have both inputs and outputs, they are mixed into Processors.

[extension/graph.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.js) defines actual Node types and their display labels.

## Required implementation

1. Introduce a single maintainable **category mapping/classification** separate from the generic number-of-ports heuristic. Explicitly map AI inference types to **AI Models**; ensure this includes all current local inference types and future AI types. Avoid classifying based solely on substring matching a Node label or on whether model assets are bundled/downloaded.
2. Explicitly categorize special non-inference types correctly: `TextFormatter`, `Hold` and other deterministic transformations remain **Processors**, `Text`, `Number`, `Button` and capture nodes are **Sources / inputs**, and visual/audio sinks are **Outputs**.
3. Remove `Constants / utilities` from the selector and results. Use a stable category order: **Sources / inputs → AI Models → Processors → Outputs → Subgraphs**. Preserve **All categories** as the category-selector option.
4. Sort **per category by visible label** automatically, including dynamically registered subgraphs. Sorting must be independent of `NODE_TYPES` definition order, node IDs and the order returned by the Graph Library.
5. Preserve filtering/search: category dropdown and query can be combined, categories retain this order, and matching items within each are sorted consistently, including mixed Latin and Japanese labels.
6. The category selection is only an **Add Node UI presentation concern**: do not change Node type IDs, graph JSON, serialization, ports, graph-validation behavior, model asset preparation, execution, existing saved graphs or subgraph definitions.
7. Do not regress the compact Add Node picker work in [#356](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/356): no result-count banner, preserve only the existing zero-results feedback, and keep compact list rows.
8. Update relevant automated UI/unit tests and any documentation that explains category selection. Do not introduce manual-human-signoff acceptance gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add Node category selector offers **All categories**, **Sources / inputs**, **AI Models**, **Processors**, **Outputs**, **Subgraphs**, and **does not offer Constants / utilities**.
- [ ] All existing AI-inference Nodes appear in **AI Models**, including ASR, translation, summarization, condition AI and TTS; deterministic text/data transformation Nodes appear in **Processors**.
- [ ] Text and Number are in **Sources / inputs**; Text formatter and Hold are in **Processors**; outputs and subgraphs are correctly grouped.
- [ ] When showing all categories, the group order is always Sources / inputs → AI Models → Processors → Outputs → Subgraphs.
- [ ] Every category's entries appear alphabetically / Japanese gojūon by the **displayed Node name**. New Node types or subgraphs naturally sort into position without maintaining array order.
- [ ] Filtering by category and searching by name continue to work together; empty results still show `No matching nodes`.
- [ ] Existing graphs and node behavior are unchanged; pointer/keyboard picker interactions and accessibility remain intact.
- [ ] Automated regression tests cover expected type→category mapping, Latin/Japanese name sorting, dynamic subgraphs, mixed query/category filtering, and absence of Constants / utilities.

## Scope

Only Add Node classification and ordering. No category descriptions, new model/processing behavior, sort controls or manual sorting settings.
